explanation: Matches the 'in particular' question on erdosproblems.com/1207 with the positive answer of Lee–Pohoata–Zhu: P_2(n) < n^{1-c} for some c > 0 and all large n. P_d(n) is the minimum, over n-point sets, of the largest isosceles-free subset. IsIsosceles only requires two equal side lengths, so equally spaced collinear triples count as isosceles. This matches the docstring's note that LPZ's isosceles-free subsets also exclude such degenerate triples, so the cited result applies to exactly this notion.
